notes: Contract dispute over indemnity obligations for pipeline right-of-way/co-tenancy revenues; court construes 'rent payments' as a contract term for a pumping-station easement dispute, not compensated occupancy of a dwelling. No lodger/boarder or short-term letting issue.
Dispute over ownership of mineral executive/leasing rights in a residential subdivision and duty owed by executive to non-executive mineral owners. No residential letting or lodging issue at all.

Premises-liability suit over an injury from a falling air-conditioning unit at a mobile office unit (MOU) being refurbished on the plaintiff's storage lot; invitee/licensee analysis is about the MOU-owner's contractor relationship, not residential letting.
Negligence suit over cattle straying onto a highway from land leased for grazing (cattle lease with hunting-rights reservations). No compensated dwelling occupancy or lodging issue.

Involves an ordinary multi-month residential lease of a 'rent house' (Melton to the Pages), but the case is entirely about premises-liability duties (invitee status, negligent failure to secure a barn that caught fire) and the Texas Tort Claims Act, not the legal character of the letting arrangement itself or short-term/lodging doctrine.

FELA/negligence suit by a railroad brakeman injured on a spur track near fertilizer-unloading operations; commercial side-track lease and indemnity provisions are between businesses (railroad, fertilizer companies), not compensated dwelling occupancy.
Forcible-detainer/breach-of-lease dispute over a convenience-store commercial lease (renewal option, fire-damage termination clause). No residential lodging/short-term letting at issue.
Personal-injury suit by a swimmer who dove off a city seawall into marina waters; licensee/invitee status analysis concerns recreational use of city property, unrelated to letting of dwellings.

Constructive-eviction case involving a commercial lease of office space to a gynecologist for an abortion practice, disrupted by anti-abortion protestors. The 'rooming house' language in the retrieved text is from a citation to a different case (Downtown Realty) within the opinion, not the facts of this case; no lodging/boarding issue here.

Criminal burglary appeal turning on whether a vacant 'rent house' used for storage qualifies as a statutory 'habitation' for enhanced burglary punishment. This is a criminal-law definitional dispute about occupancy/adaptation for overnight use, not a civil doctrine case on the legality or characterization of short-term letting; no lodger/boarder relationship at issue.

Invalidates a city ordinance requiring neighboring-property-owner consent to site a mobile/travel trailer park as an unlawful delegation of police power. Concerns siting of trailer parks (a distinct land-use category), not licensing/regulation of room letting or lodging/boarding houses within a dwelling; borderline but not squarely on the pipeline's doctrine.

Wrongful-death/Tort Claims Act suit after a state-hospital patient drowned during a supervised outing at a hospital lake facility. No letting/lodging issue; invitee/licensee/trespasser analysis relates to use of hospital recreational property.

Premises-liability suit by a pest-control worker injured by a syringe in a restaurant restroom; invitee-status analysis is about scope of a service contractor's business invitation, unrelated to dwelling letting.
Trespass-to-try-title and bad-faith-trespass dispute over oil-and-gas mineral cotenancy and an unauthorized lease of a co-owned mineral estate. No compensated dwelling occupancy issue.
Capital-murder appeal (shooting at a football-game parking lot); a 'rent house' owned by the landowner defendants is mentioned only as an unrelated location detail. No letting/lodging issue.

Gift-deed/constructive-trust dispute over 153 acres of land; a 'rent house' on the tract is mentioned only in passing (grantee collected rent from it briefly). No doctrinal discussion of letting arrangements.

Declaratory-judgment action holding a city ordinance's construction-standard restriction on installing manufactured homes preempted by state wind-zone law. Concerns siting/construction standards for owner-occupied manufactured homes, not compensated letting of dwelling space to occupants.
Substantive-due-course-of-law challenge to cosmetology licensing requirements for eyebrow threaders. No connection to residential letting, lodging, or boarding houses.
